description: American Indian Culture (formerly Indian Lore) is a respectful study of the cultural areas, nations and present-day life of American Indian peoples: one tribe or nation in depth, language and place names, leaders, contributions, games, museums and gatherings.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Scouting America renamed Indian Lore to American Indian Culture; the official note says the curriculum and requirements were otherwise unchanged by the rename. Confirm whether requirement 5 asks for one or both options.

American Indian Culture merit badge (formerly Indian Lore)

requirements.title: Cultural areas
requirements.summary: The different American Indian cultural areas and what makes each distinct.

requirements.title: Researching a nation
requirements.summary: The way of life, government, beliefs, language, arts and present-day communities of one tribe, group or nation.

requirements.title: Language, places, and leaders
requirements.summary: Words in an American Indian language, the meanings of place names, and notable leaders and their contributions.

requirements.title: Contributions and games
requirements.summary: How American Indians shaped life for newcomers, things others adopted from American Indian cultures, and teaching a traditional game.

requirements.title: Museums and gatherings
requirements.summary: Visiting a museum to study artifacts, or attending a contemporary American Indian gathering and learning its etiquette.
